title: Rizogalo (rice pudding)
ingredients:
1 ½ cups caster sugar
1 ¼ cups medium grain rice
2 litres milk
1 tablespoon vanilla extract
ground cinnamon, for dusting
steps:
In a large saucepan, add the sugar, rice and milk. Bring to the boil, stirring frequently, then reduce the heat while still stirring. Simmer, stirring frequently, for about 45 minutes or until the rice is cooked and the pudding texture is thick.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
Pour into little pudding bowls or one big serving dish. Sprinkle with cinnamon, cool at room temperature then serve.

title: Baked snapper and vegetables
ingredients:
1 whole snapper (about 1 kg)
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
juice of 1 lemon
1 onion, sliced
3 tomatoes, sliced
⅓ cup fresh parsley leaves
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Brush the fish with the olive oil in a baking dish. Season with salt and pepper, then squeeze lemon juice over.
Scatter the onion and tomato over the fish, followed by the parsley and bake until the fish is cooked, about 25 minutes.
Serve with baked seasonal vegetables.

title: Pilafi (beef and rice)
ingredients:
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, finely chopped
6 cloves garlic, crushed
500 grams lean beef, diced
salt and pepper
250 grams diced tomato
1 capsicum, deseeded and chopped
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
1 ½ cups medium grain rice (see note)
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion and garlic until the onion is translucent. Add the beef and cook on a high heat for about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then add the tomato and cook until soft. Add the capsicum and parsley. Add the rice and cover with 1 ½ cups water. Bring to the boil then cover and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Serve with feta or Homemade tzatziki and salad.
When I make this dish today, I use brown basmati rice.

title: Roast lamb and pasta – the perfect Sunday lunch
ingredients:
2.5 kg leg of lamb on the bone
10 cloves garlic, 4 crushed
2 tablespoons tomato paste
salt and pepper
1 cup white wine
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 onions, sliced
juice of 1 lemon
1 tablespoon dried oregano
5 cups beef stock
500 grams pasta
450 grams ripe tomatoes
handful of fresh oregano, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Pierce the lamb leg with about 6 garlic cloves, pushing the cloves deep into the meat. Rub the lamb with the tomato paste and salt and pepper, then place in a roasting pan. Cover with the wine, olive oil, onion, lemon juice and the crushed garlic. Sprinkle the oregano over the top.
Add 3 cups of the stock to the roasting pan, cover with foil and bake for 1 ½ hours.
Remove the pan from the oven and turn the meat over in the dish. Bring the remaining stock to the boil and add to the roasting pan. Add the pasta and the tomatoes and return to the oven for about 45 minutes. Check periodically; if the pasta is looking uncooked, add some water.
Remove from the oven and give the pasta a stir to make sure all the meat juices are mixed through.
Serve with Greek salad and a garnish of fresh oregano.

title: Papou’s spanakorizo (spinach and rice)
ingredients:

5 cloves garlic, crushed
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 bunch English spinach, chopped
1 bunch dill, chopped
juice and zest of 2 lemons
1 ½ cups basmati rice
750 ml chicken stock
250 grams feta, crumbled
1 bunch parsley, chopped
steps:
Cook the onion and garlic in the olive oil in a large pot until the onion is translucent. Add the spinach and dill, cooking until the spinach wilts. Add the lemon zest, rice and stock. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer until the rice is cooked through.
Add the feta, lemon juice and parsley and cover for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Stuffed tomatoes
ingredients:
1 cup basmati rice
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
500 grams beef mince
salt and pepper
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon ground cinnamon
½ teaspoon ground nutmeg
1 x 400-gram can crushed tomatoes
½ cup white wine
1 cup chopped fresh parsley
¼ cup chopped fresh mint
6 large tomatoes
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Give the rice a good rinse.
For the stuffing, in a large frying pan, cook the olive oil, onion and garlic until translucent. Add the beef, salt and pepper, cumin, oregano, cinnamon and nutmeg. Cook for a few minutes.
When the meat is browned, add the rice, canned tomatoes, wine and ¼ cup water. Bring to the boil and let simmer for 15 minutes. Add the fresh herbs and salt and pepper to taste.
For the tomatoes, cut off the top of each tomato and set aside. Scoop out the flesh, creating a cavity for the filling. Chop the flesh and set aside.
Prepare a baking pan by brushing it with olive oil then sprinkle the tomato flesh over the base of the pan. Add the filling to the tomato cavities and arrange on the baking dish. Put the reserved top on each tomato.
Pour ¾ cup water into the baking dish. Generously drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle some salt over the dish. Cover the dish with foil and bake in the oven for 45 minutes, or until you can see the rice is cooked.
Take care not to overcook because the tomatoes will collapse.

Slowly drizzle in the olive oil and incorporate everything to create a paste.

title: Sarah’s Kythera spanakopita
ingredients:

1 onion, grated

¼ cup chopped fresh dill
¼ cup chopped fresh mint

salt and pepper
4 eggs
10 sheets filo pastry
steps:

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the spring onions and onion until translucent.
Next, mix the remaining ingredients together and add to onion mix.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil then line with a sheet of pastry. Brush the pastry with olive oil. Repeat with another 4 sheets of pastry. Add the spinach mixture to the baking dish then top with another 5 sheets of pastry, brushing each sheet with oil. Finally, brush the top with olive oil. Bake in the oven for 1 hour.

title: Melitzanosalata (smoky grilled eggplant dip)
ingredients:
2 large eggplants
⅓ cup chopped red onion, plus extra to serve
3 cloves garlic, crushed
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
juice and zest of 1 lemon, plus extra zest to serve
1 cup chopped fresh parsley
pinch of chilli powder (optional)
½ teaspoon cumin
salt and pepper
feta, olives and parsley, to serve
steps:
Pierce the eggplants with a fork and grill, turning until the skin is charred and eggplants are soft and cooked. Cool, drain off any liquid and set aside.
Peel the eggplants and cut the flesh into chunks. Put the chunks in a tea towel and squeeze to remove any extra liquid.
Add the eggplant to a mixing bowl with the onion, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice and zest, parsley, spices, and salt and pepper. Mix well with a fork, then cover and put in the fridge for 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, garnish with lemon zest, chopped red onion, feta, olives and parsley.

title: Grilled octopus

salt

steps:

Remove from the pot and drain well.
Sprinkle the octopus with salt, then with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Cover.
Mix the remaining olive oil with the juice of 1 lemon. Cut the other lemon into wedges for serving. Grill or BBQ the octopus for a few minutes on each side over a medium-high heat. Squeeze a little lemon juice over, drizzle with the oil, and sprinkle with oregano and lemon wedges.

salt and pepper

steps:

title: Garlic sauce
ingredients:
⅔ cup garlic cloves
salt
juice of 1 lemon
2 cups sunflower oil (see note)
¼ cup cold water
steps:

Keeping the motor running, slowly drizzle in the oil. Once you’ve added about one-quarter of it, add a little bit of the water then slowly alternate between water and oil. Eventually, the sauce will become smooth. Be patient because this process can take about 10 minutes.
As garlic sauce has a strong flavour I prefer to use sunflower oil in this recipe. Even though sunflower oil is higher in omega 6 than olive oil, it is fine occasionally in a healthy balanced diet where the omega 3 to 6 ratio is balanced.

title: Falafels
ingredients:
1 cup dried chickpeas
½ teaspoon baking soda
3 cloves garlic, crushed
½ cup chopped fresh coriander
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
⅓ cup chopped spring onions
1 teaspoon ground cumin
½ teaspoon ground coriander
pinch of sea salt and black pepper
2 tablespoons wholemeal flour
½ teaspoon baking powder
extra-virgin olive oil, for frying
steps:
Place the chickpeas and baking soda in a large bowl. Cover completely with water and soak overnight.
The next day drain the chickpeas and pat dry. Place in a food processor along with the garlic, herbs, spring onions, spices, and salt and pepper and blitz to form a paste.
Combine the flour and baking powder and stir into the mixture. Check the consistency and add a little more flour if necessary.
Take 1 heaped tablespoon of the falafel mixture and form into a ball. Repeat with the remaining mixture. Place the balls on a plate and chill for 30 minutes in the fridge.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan. Add the chilled balls and press them into disc shapes. Cook for about 3 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Serve with Homemade tzatziki or Homemade hummus .

steps:

Meanwhile, cook the onion and garlic in the extra olive oil in a soup pot until translucent.
Add the tomato mixture and cook over medium heat for a few minutes. Add the canned tomatoes, herbs and spices plus 2 ½ cups water. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes.

steps:

title: Chicken and vegetable soup
ingredients:
6 chicken thighs with bone
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 carrots, chopped
1 onion, chopped
5 cloves garlic, crushed
1 teaspoon sea salt
1 litre chicken stock
1 broccoli head, chopped
2 small zucchini, chopped
½ small cauliflower, trimmed and chopped
fresh herbs of your choice, to serve
steps:
Add the chicken thighs and 1 litre water to a large pot. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large casserole dish. Add the carrot, onion, garlic and salt then cook for a few minutes.
Remove any scum from the top of the chicken water. Transfer the chicken and water to the casserole dish then add the chicken stock. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and cook for 3 hours.
Remove the chicken and shred the meat off the bones. Return the shredded chicken to the dish, add the vegetables and cook for another 20 minutes.
When the soup is ready, serve with a big garnish of fresh herbs of your choice.

title: Greek lentil soup

salt and pepper

steps:

Put the olive oil, onion, carrot and garlic in a pan and cook until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the lentils, 1 litre water and herbs. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, season with salt and pepper, and cook for another 30 minutes. Drizzle with the red wine vinegar and extra olive oil to serve.

title: Fish, tomato and basil soup

1 kg fish fillets, chopped

salt and pepper, to serve
steps:

Add the fish and cook for 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Serve with a garnish of fresh basil and season with salt and pepper.

title: Fasolakia (green bean stew)

1 x 400-gram can whole tomatoes
2 potatoes, cut into small pieces
1 bay leaf
salt and pepper
juice of 1 lemon
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
steps:
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Heat ¼ cup olive oil in an ovenproof casserole dish. Add the onion, garlic, oregano and cumin. Cook for a few minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes, potato, bay leaf and 1 cup water. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Cover the casserole dish and put into the oven. Cook for 30 minutes, until the potatoes are cooked through.
Remove from the oven. Serve with a squeeze of lemon juice, chopped parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Turmeric chicken soup
ingredients:
1 ¼ litres chicken stock
500 grams chicken breast fillets
1 white or brown onion, chopped
6 cloves garlic, crushed
salt and pepper
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 carrots, sliced
1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon ground turmeric
2 cups chopped English spinach
1 cup chopped fresh parsley
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
juice and zest of 1 lemon
steps:
Add the stock to a deep saucepan. Add the chicken, onion, half the garlic, and salt and pepper to taste. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer until the chicken is cooked, about 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken and shred it.
Strain the liquid from the saucepan and set aside along with the cooked onion and garlic. Wipe the pot clean then add the olive oil, carrot, remaining garlic and spices. Heat and stir for a couple of minutes. Return the shredded chicken, cooked onion and garlic to the pot along with the strained broth. Cook on a medium heat for 15 minutes.
When ready to serve, stir through the spinach, herbs, and lemon juice and zest.

salt and pepper
500 grams salmon, cut into cubes
juice and zest of 1 lemon
handful of chopped fresh parsley, to serve
steps:

Add the dill, stock, potato, carrot, herbs and spices, and salt and pepper. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes until the potato is cooked.
Add the salmon, lemon juice and zest, and cook for 5 minutes.

title: Pea and carrot stew
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil

steps:

title: Traditional Greek beef soup

salt and pepper
handful of fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a soup pot and brown the meat. Remove the meat from the pot, add 2 litres water and bring to the boil.

Serve with the parsley.

title: Youvarlakia (Greek meatball soup)
ingredients:
8 cups water
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
½ teaspoon sea salt
steps:
For the broth, put all the ingredients in a large soup pot and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 15 minutes.
For the meatballs, combine all the ingredients and mix together well. Roll spoonfuls of mixture about the size of an apricot into little meatballs in the palm of your hand. Be sure to roll them tight so they don’t break apart during cooking. You should get about 40 from the mixture.
Transfer the meatballs to the simmering broth and cook for about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the avgolemono. Separate the eggs, placing the whites in a mixing bowl and the yolks in another bowl. Whisk the whites until fluffy. Then add the yolks and lemon juice, whisking until incorporated.
When the meatballs are cooked, take some broth from the meatballs and slowly whisk into your egg mixture, and repeat one more time. Add this mixture back into the soup and stir through, it will look foamy. Turn off the heat and let the soup sit for about 15 minutes until it reaches a thick consistency.

file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

steps:

title: Fish soup

handful of fresh dill, to serve
steps:

Serve the soup with the sauce poured over and garnish with dill.

title: Kapsali bean salad

title: Pumpkin roast
ingredients:

1 capsicum, cut in half lengthwise and deseeded

steps:

Drizzle the pumpkin with some olive oil, wrap in foil and roast in the oven for 30 minutes.
Open the oven and place the egglant, zucchini and capsicum on the tray, drizzle with oil and roast for another 30 minutes.
When ready, discard capsicum skin and slice capsicum into strips. Scoop out the flesh from inside the pumpkin and set aside, leaving a border around the edge.
Toast the pistachios in a dry frying pan until golden. Add the leek, garlic, 1 cup pumpkin flesh, basil, and salt and pepper. Stir well.
Place the pumpkin skin-side down and fill the cavities with the vegetable mixture. Top with the roasted eggplant, zucchini and capsicum.
Put the pumpkin back together, tying with kitchen string then covering with plastic wrap. Place in the fridge overnight.
The next day, preheat the oven to 180°C. Remove the plastic wrap and place the pumpkin on a lined baking tray. Add the tomatoes around it and roast for 25 minutes.
Slice the pumpkin into discs and serve with extra pistachios and basil.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Roasted baby carrots with chilli and hummus
ingredients:
250 grams baby carrots
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
250 grams Homemade hummus
3 spring onions, chopped
1 lime, cut into wedges, to serve
chilli flakes, to serve
steps:
Preheat the grill. Toss the carrots in olive oil and grill for 4 minutes on each side.
For the dressing, put the ingredients in a jar and shake well.
Spread the hummus on a platter. Arrange the carrots on top, then drizzle with the dressing and garnish with spring onion and lime wedges. Sprinkle with chilli flakes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Bread and avocado salad
ingredients:
4 cups chopped ripe tomatoes
1 avocado, chopped
1 red onion, diced
2 cloves garlic, crushed
2 tablespoons capers
1 loaf sourdough bread
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 cups chopped fresh basil leaves
2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar
pepper
steps:
Put the tomato, avocado, onion, garlic and capers in a bowl and mix together.
In a serving dish, break up the bread into bite-sized pieces and drizzle with half the olive oil.
Add the basil leaves and top with the tomato mixture. Drizzle with the vinegar and remaining olive oil. Season with pepper and enjoy.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Cauliflower and broccoli health bowls
ingredients:
1 cup broccoli florets
1 cup cauliflower florets
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
1 cup cooked quinoa (cook as you would rice in boiling water)
2 cups baby spinach
2 cooked beetroot (fresh or canned), chopped
12 walnuts, chopped
juice of 1 lemon
¼ cup Homemade hummus
chilli flakes (optional)
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place the broccoli and cauliflower on the tray, drizzle with half the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 20 minutes.
When ready, remove from the oven.
To prepare the bowls, place half the quinoa in the bottom of each bowl. Add the spinach, beetroot, and roasted cauliflower and broccoli. Sprinkle with the walnuts and squeeze the lemon juice over the top. Add the hummus, sprinkle with chilli flakes if using, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and sprinkle with parsley.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean vegetable stew
ingredients:
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
4 sprigs fresh thyme
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon sweet paprika
3 celery stalks, chopped
2 carrots, chopped
2 capsicums, chopped
1 cup vegetable stock
4 cups chopped cherry tomatoes
2 zucchini, sliced
1 cup cooked lentils
salt and pepper
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a casserole dish and cook the onion and garlic for a few minutes.
Add the herbs and spices, celery, carrot and capsicum, and cook for a few minutes.
Add the stock, cherry tomatoes and zucchini and cook for 20 minutes. Add the lentils in the last 5 minutes of cooking time, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with crusty fresh sourdough bread, rice or cauliflower rice.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Lentil ragu with zucchini noodles
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
4 celery stalks, chopped
2 carrots, chopped
1 onion, chopped
6 cloves garlic, crushed
2 cups chopped mushrooms
1 tablespoon dried oregano
500 grams dried brown lentils
500 grams passata
1 litre vegetable stock
2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
4 zucchini, spiralised
fresh oregano or parsley, to serve
salt and pepper, to serve
steps:
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the celery, carrot, onion, garlic, mushrooms and oregano for about 5 minutes.
Add the lentils, passata, stock and vinegar. Cover and cook on a low heat for about 25 minutes.
Just before serving, add the zucchini to a frying pan with a dash of olive oil and cook for a few minutes.
Serve immediately, garnished with oregano or parsley and seasoned with salt and pepper.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Okra stew
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
5 cloves garlic, crushed
2 green jalapeño chillies, deseeded and chopped
500 grams okra, trimmed
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon sweet paprika
salt and pepper
2 cups chopped tomatoes
juice of 1 lemon
handful of fresh coriander, to serve
steps:
Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a pan. Add the onion, garlic and jalapeños, cooking over medium heat. Add the okra and spices, season with salt and pepper, and stir through. Add the tomatoes and ½ cup water, bring to the boil then reduce the heat, letting it simmer for 20 minutes.
When ready to serve, squeeze lemon juice over the top, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and garnish with coriander.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Tomato rice cups
ingredients:
8 large tomatoes
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil
3 onions, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
⅔ cup rice
¼ cup tomato paste
1 cup chopped fresh parsley
salt and pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cut the tops off the tomatoes, remove the seeds and scoop out the flesh. Chop the flesh and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a frying pan. Cook the onion and garlic until the onion is translucent.
Add the rice, the chopped tomato flesh and tomato paste. Bring to the boil then reduce heat and simmer for about 5 minutes. Stir in the parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Put the hollowed-out tomatoes in a deep baking dish and add the mixture to the cavities. Drizzle with olive oil.
Pour ½ cup water into the dish, cover the tomatoes with foil and bake for 30 minutes or until the rice is cooked.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Broad beans with artichokes and peas
ingredients:
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 onions, sliced
4 cloves garlic, crushed
250 grams broad beans (canned is fine)
juice of 1 lemon
1 cup frozen peas
400 grams artichoke hearts (jarred is fine)
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
¼ cup chopped fresh mint
4 spring onions, chopped
salt and pepper
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and garlic, stirring well. Add the beans, lemon juice and ½ cup water. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the peas, artichoke hearts, herbs and spring onion. Season with salt and pepper, and simmer until the peas are cooked.
Serve and enjoy.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean roasted lemon and rosemary artichokes
ingredients:
6 artichokes (see note)
3 lemons, cut in half
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
fresh rosemary sprigs
salt and pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut off the base of each artichoke so it can stand upright. Fan open the leaves, rub the lemons all over to stop the artichokes browning, then paint them with the olive oil. Sprinkle the rosemary sprigs over the top plus a generous amount of sea salt and black pepper. Bake in the oven for 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven, cover with foil and bake for another 20 minutes until the artichokes are tender.
We always enjoyed artichokes just as described in this recipe, but you could make a dipping sauce, or dunk artichoke leaves in a garlic, hummus, taramasalata or tzatziki dip.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Green beans in oil
ingredients:
1 kg green beans, ends trimmed
1 onion, chopped
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil
4 ripe tomatoes, skinned and crushed
salt and pepper
steps:
Put the beans in a saucepan with the onion and ½ cup water. Cook until the onion is soft.
Add the olive oil, tomatoes, and salt and pepper. Add another 1 cup water. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Homemade hummus
ingredients:
1 x 400-gram can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
juice of 1 lemon
1 clove garlic, crushed
¼ cup tahini
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 tablespoons water
½ teaspoon ground cumin
salt
steps: Put all the ingredients in a food processor and blitz to combine.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Italian vegetables
ingredients:
350 grams baby potatoes, cut into cubes
extra-virgin olive oil, for drizzling
3 cups chopped cherry tomatoes
1 cup chopped mushrooms
2 zucchini, chopped
12 cloves garlic, crushed
1 tablespoon fresh or dried oregano
1 teaspoon fresh or dried thyme
salt and pepper
grated parmesan cheese, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. As the potatoes take longer to cook, put them in a baking dish with a drizzle of olive oil and roast for 10–12 minutes.
Remove from the oven, add the other vegetables, garlic and herbs, season with salt and pepper, and return to the oven for another 15–20 minutes.
When ready, scatter the parmesan over the top and serve.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Pumpkin and chickpea delight
ingredients:
1 cup pitted dates
1 kg pumpkin, cut into 5 cm pieces
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 x 400-gram cans chickpeas, rinsed and drained
½ cup Spanish olives
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
salt and pepper
1 tablespoon pepitas
½ cup chopped fresh coriander
steps:
Soak the dates in boiling water until soft, about 5 minutes.
Brown the pumpkin pieces in a frying pan with the olive oil.
Add the dates, chickpeas, olives, 1 cup water, cinnamon, and salt and pepper then cook for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is cooked.
Serve with pepitas and fresh coriander scattered over the top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Veggie, bean and pistachio pesto
ingredients:
1 large eggplant, sliced lengthwise as thinly as possible
2 zucchini, sliced lengthwise
1 cup cherry tomatoes
1 x 400-gram can cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
salt and pepper
steps:
For the pesto, put all the ingredients in a food processor and blitz until smooth.
Grill the eggplant, zucchini and tomatoes for best results; otherwise, cook them in a frying pan for a few minutes only – you don’t want them overcooked.
Spread the cannellini beans on a platter. Cover with the vegetables and dollop the pesto over. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with some fresh basil leaves and a sprinkle of pistachios.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: French ratatouille
ingredients:
5 tomatoes
4 capsicums
3 medium-sized zucchini
2 eggplants
2 onions
6 cloves garlic, crushed
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1 teaspoon dried dill
salt and pepper
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
fresh basil and oregano, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking dish with baking paper.
Slice all your vegetables crosswise, not lengthwise, so you have lots of discs on your chopping board.
Put all the vegetables in a bowl and toss with the garlic, dried herbs, and salt and pepper to taste. Pour in the olive oil and toss.
Layer alternating slices of vegetables in the baking dish, overlapping slightly. If you have a round dish, layer the vegetables in a circle; if you have a square or rectangular dish, make uniform rows. Cover with foil and bake for about 45–50 minutes.
Once the vegetables are tender, remove from the oven and scatter with fresh basil and oregano.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Zucchini and rice
ingredients:
4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
400 grams zucchini, chopped (keep the skin on)
⅓ cup basmati rice
1 cup chopped tomatoes (or 1 x 400-gram can crushed tomatoes)
1 tablespoon dried mint
1 teaspoon maple syrup
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
salt and pepper
fresh lemon wedges, to serve
crumbled feta, to serve (optional)
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a pot then add the onion and sauté. Add the zucchini and rice, giving it a stir to make sure the oil is covering everything.
Add the tomatoes, mint, maple syrup and ¼ cup water. Cover and cook for about 20 minutes or until the rice is cooked.
Add the dill and salt and pepper to taste then cook for a few minutes more.
Serve with lemon wedges and/or some feta.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Lemon rice
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
1 cup basmati rice
2 cups vegetable stock
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
salt and pepper
juice and zest of 1 lemon
steps:
Heat the oil in a pot then cook the onion until translucent. Add the rice and stock, stirring together, then reduce the heat and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.
Stir through the parsley, salt and pepper, and lemon juice and zest, then serve.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Pastitsio
ingredients:
450 grams penne pasta
2 egg whites
120 grams feta, crumbled
salt and pepper
steps:
For the meat sauce, add the onion and olive oil to a casserole dish and sauté. Add the beef, garlic and tomato paste and cook until the mince is browned.
Add the red wine, canned tomatoes, maple syrup, cinnamon, clove and bay leaf. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and let simmer for about 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
For the bechamel, put the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the flour and make a paste, then slowly add the milk to thicken.
Remove from the heat then add the egg yolks, grated cheese, nutmeg, and salt and pepper to taste.
Cook the pasta but be careful not to overcook it, even leave it slightly undercooked. Drain and add the egg whites and feta, seasoning with salt and pepper and mixing well.
Grab a rectangular baking dish, about 25 cm by 35 cm. Assemble with a layer of pasta first, then the meat sauce and finally the bechamel. Sprinkle with grated cheese and bake for 15–20 minutes until golden brown.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Spanakorizo (spinach and rice)
ingredients:
500 grams fresh spinach, rinsed and chopped
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
juice of ½ lemon, plus extra to serve (optional)
2 spring onions, chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill
1 tablespoon chopped fresh mint, plus extra whole leaves to serve
⅓ cup basmati rice
salt and pepper
grated parmesan cheese, to serve (optional)
crumbled feta, to serve (optional)
steps:
Wilt the spinach with the olive oil and lemon juice in a large pot over a medium heat. In another pot, sauté the onion. Add the wilted spinach and herbs plus ⅔ cup water and bring to the boil. Add the rice and salt and pepper to taste, then cover and cook for 20 minutes. Check on the dish during cooking, you may need to add more water along the way.
Serve with an extra drizzle of olive oil and fresh mint leaves. I love this recipe with grated fresh parmesan cheese on top, but a good squeeze of fresh lemon juice also works beautifully. Crumbled feta over the top is also sensational.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Rice with leek – the perfect side
ingredients:
500 grams chopped leeks (white and pale green parts only)
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
⅓ cup basmati rice
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
1 tablespoon tomato paste
1 ⅓ cups boiling water
salt and pepper
steps:
Blanch the chopped leek in boiling water for a few minutes then strain.
Heat the olive oil in a pot on medium heat and sauté the leeks. Add the rice, dill, tomato paste and boiling water. Season with salt and pepper, mixing together well.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes. Keep checking because you may need to give it a stir or add a little more water.
Serve as a side dish or as a main with some feta.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Cabbage and rice
ingredients:
1 onion, chopped
4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
½ cabbage, shredded
2 teaspoons tomato paste
salt and pepper
½ cup basmati rice (or medium-grain rice for a more risotto-like consistency)
freshly squeezed lemon juice and fresh parsley, to serve (or whatever fresh herbs you like)
chilli flakes, to serve (optional)
crumbled feta, to serve (optional)
steps:
Sauté the onion for about 5 minutes in the olive oil.
Add the cabbage and sauté for a couple of minutes. Then add 1 cup hot water, cover and let the cabbage simmer for 20 minutes.
Loosen the tomato paste with ¼ cup water and add to the pot with salt and pepper to taste, giving it all a mix. Add the rice and 1 ½ cups water and cook for about 15–20 minutes.
Serve with lemon juice and parsley, or herbs of your choice. Chilli flakes work well too or you could add some feta.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Beef rice pilaf
ingredients:
1 kg beef chuck steak, diced
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
2 carrots, grated
1 onion, diced
10 cloves garlic, crushed
1 litre beef stock
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
2 cups basmati rice
chopped fresh herbs, to serve
steps:
Put the beef in a casserole dish with the oil and sear it on all sides. Season with salt and pepper, remove from the dish and set aside.
Add the carrot, onion and garlic to the dish and cook for a few minutes. Return the beef to the dish, mix to combine and cook for a few minutes. Add the stock and spices and cook the beef over low heat for about 1 hour to cook through.
Stir through the rice, cover and cook for another 30 minutes.
When ready to serve, mix well and garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Roasted vegetable couscous
ingredients:
1 carrot, diced
1 zucchini, chopped
1 onion, diced
1 capsicum, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
1 x 400-gram can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. For the roasted vegetables, mix the carrot, zucchini, onion, capsicum and garlic with the olive oil. Spread over a baking tray, season with salt and pepper, and roast in the oven for 20 minutes.
For the couscous, boil the stock, pour over the couscous in a bowl and cover for 5 minutes. Fluff up with a fork and set aside.
For the dressing, put all the ingredients in a jar and shake well.
To serve, stir the fresh herbs through the couscous, then add the roasted vegetables and chickpeas and combine. Add the dressing and serve.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
serves: SERVES 2 AS A MAIN OR 4 AS A SIDE DISH

title: Couscous and tuna salad
ingredients:
½ cup couscous
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
2 cups chopped fresh parsley
1 cup chopped cherry tomatoes
3 cloves garlic, chopped
1 x 185-gram can tuna in oil, drained
salt and pepper
100 grams feta, crumbled
lemon wedges, to serve
steps:
Place the couscous in a bowl with ½ cup boiling water, 1 teaspoon olive oil and a pinch of salt, and stir lightly. Cover and let sit for about 5 minutes, or until the couscous has absorbed all the water. Add the parsley.
Sauté the tomatoes in a pan with the garlic and remaining olive oil, cooking for a few minutes or until the tomatoes soften. Add the cooked tomatoes and tuna to the couscous and toss together. Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil, crumble feta over the top and serve with lemon wedges.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Caprese pasta salad
ingredients:
1 cup pulse pasta (you can use whatever pasta you like)
150 grams bocconcini
1 cup cherry tomatoes
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
handful of basil leaves
salt and pepper
balsamic vinegar glaze, to serve
steps:
Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions.
Put the cooked pasta, bocconcini, cherry tomatoes and olive oil in a salad bowl and toss together. Add the basil leaves, salt and pepper to taste, and balsamic glaze over the top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Tuna pasta salad
ingredients:
300 grams spaghetti
2 cups frozen peas
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
1 capsicum, chopped
6 cloves garlic, crushed
juice and zest of 1 lemon
1 cup chopped fresh parsley, plus extra to serve
1 teaspoon dried oregano
1 x 400-gram can tuna in oil, drained
½ cup pitted chopped olives
grated parmesan cheese, to serve
steps:
Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions, adding the frozen peas into the pasta water in the last 2 minutes. Drain, setting aside about ½ cup of the pasta water.
In a frying pan, add the oil, capsicum and garlic and cook. Add the cooked pasta, lemon juice and zest, parsley and oregano, tossing together. Next, add the tuna and olives, mixing in the pan over medium heat for just a few minutes to heat through.
Serve with the extra parsley, drizzle olive oil over the top and grated parmesan.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chicken and quinoa
ingredients:
1 cup quinoa
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
4 chicken breast fillets
1 pomegranate, seeds only
1 cucumber, chopped
30 grams pistachios
balsamic vinegar glaze, to serve
bunch of fresh mint, to serve
50 grams feta, crumbled, to serve
steps:
Cook the quinoa as per the packet instructions, adding the olive oil and salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken by grilling, frying or barbecuing.
When the quinoa is cooked, toss through the pomegranate seeds, cucumber and pistachios. Place in a serving dish. Slice the chicken and place over the quinoa.
Serve with balsamic vinegar glaze drizzled over the chicken. Scatter with mint and crumbled feta.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Beef risoni
ingredients:
5 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 carrots, chopped
1 red onion, chopped
1 kg diced beef
2 tablespoons tomato paste
1 cup beef stock
1 cup chopped cherry tomatoes
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon maple syrup
salt and pepper
2 cups risoni
125 grams feta, to serve
fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Add 2 tablespoons of olive oil to a casserole dish and sauté the carrot and onion. Add the beef and brown it, in batches if need be.
Stir through the tomato paste and stock and cook briefly, then add the tomatoes, cinnamon, maple syrup, and salt and pepper to taste. Cover with water and simmer for about 45 minutes or until the meat looks cooked. You may need to top up with water.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a frying pan and add the risoni, stirring to coat. Tip the risoni into the meat mixture. Add 2 cups water, stir everything together, cover the dish with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Check regularly because it may need some more water.
Remove the foil and return to the oven for another 10 minutes.
When ready, serve with the feta and fresh parsley scattered over.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Tomato and feta risoni
ingredients:
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
½ brown or white onion, chopped
2 cloves garlic, crushed
1 cup risoni
1 ½ cups chopped tomatoes (or 1 x 400-gram can crushed tomatoes)
1 teaspoon dried oregano
salt and pepper
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley, to serve
scattering of feta, to serve
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and garlic for about 5 minutes until the onion is transparent.
Stir through the risoni and mix together. Next, add 2 ½ cups water, tomatoes, oregano and salt and pepper to taste. Cook, covered, for about 10–15 minutes or until the risoni is cooked.
Serve with parsley and feta scattered on top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean risoni
ingredients:
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
500 grams risoni
2 cups chopped cherry tomatoes (or 2 x 400-gram cans crushed tomatoes)
½ cup chopped kalamata olives
1 bunch fresh dill, chopped
500 ml chicken stock
1 cup chopped fresh parsley
juice of 1 lemon
salt and pepper
150 grams feta
steps:
Put the olive oil, onion and garlic in a large pan and cook until the onion is translucent.
Add the risoni, tomatoes, olives and dill, then pour in the stock. Cover, bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer until the risoni is cooked, about 10 minutes. Give the occasional stir during cooking.
Stir in the parsley, lemon juice, and salt and pepper to taste. Serve with feta crumbled over the top. Delish.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chicken pasta
ingredients:
4 cups pasta of your choice (penne works well for this)
2 chicken breast fillets
1 teaspoon dried oregano
pinch of salt and pepper
4 cloves garlic, crushed
250 grams feta, plus extra to serve
½ cup Greek yoghurt
juice of 1 lemon
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 ½ cups cherry tomatoes
½ cup pitted black olives
¼ cup chopped fresh dill
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley, plus extra to serve
steps:
Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions.
Season the chicken with oregano and salt and pepper, and cook under the grill or on the BBQ for 10 minutes or until cooked. Let rest before slicing.
Add the hot cooked pasta to a large bowl and stir through the garlic, feta, yoghurt, lemon juice and olive oil. Next, add the tomatoes, olives and fresh herbs. Toss together and serve with the sliced chicken and a sprinkle of feta and parsley.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Seasonal fruit and yoghurt with chia seeds, cinnamon and granola
ingredients:
1 cup mixed seasonal fruit (three different types)
½ cup Sarah’s granola (see below)
½ cup Greek yoghurt
½ teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 tablespoon chia seeds
¼ cup fresh mint leaves, torn
steps:
Place the fruit and granola in a breakfast bowl. Stir the cinnamon through the yoghurt then dollop over the fruit.
Sprinkle with chia seeds and mint.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Easy Mediterranean healthy lunch bowl
ingredients:
2 asparagus spears
½ cup cooked brown rice
½ cup canned butter beans
¼ avocado, chopped
½ cup grated carrot
½ cup grated beetroot
½ cup baby spinach leaves
50 grams feta, crumbled
extra-virgin olive oil, to serve
balsamic vinegar, to serve
salt and pepper
steps:

title: Mediterranean frittata

salt and pepper

steps:

title: Eggs in capsicum cups

2 capsicums
4 eggs
salt and pepper

handful of fresh coriander, to serve
steps:

Cut the capsicums in half lengthwise, removing the seeds and stem. Season with salt and pepper and roast for 10 minutes.
Crack an egg into each capsicum half, season, then sprinkle with cheese and roast until the eggs are cooked, about 15 minutes.
Serve garnished with fresh coriander.

title: Mediterranean-style breakfast bowl

½ capsicum, chopped

1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, to serve
salt and pepper

title: Beans and egg
ingredients:
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil

½ cup Greek yoghurt
juice of 1 lemon

salt and pepper
handful of fresh parsley, to serve
steps:

title: Sarah’s spring vegetable slice

title: Baked snapper
ingredients:
2 cups chopped tomatoes
6 cloves garlic, crushed
½ cup black olives
⅔ cup chicken stock
juice and zest of 2 lemons

salt and pepper

1 cup chopped fresh dill, plus extra to serve
1 cup chopped fresh oregano, plus extra to serve
1 snapper (about 1.5 kg)
steps:

Remove the baking tray from the oven, nestle the fish in among the vegetables, and return to the oven for another 15–20 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Serve with dill and oregano scattered over the top.

title: Octopus and oregano

1 cup chopped fresh dill
salt and pepper
steps:
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Add the octopus, reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drain the water, remove the octopus and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion until translucent.
Pour in the stock. Mix the tomato paste with 1 cup water and stir through, then add the octopus. Cook for about 30 minutes.

title: Scallops in capsicum sauce

handful of fresh parsley, to serve
salt and pepper

title: Baked fish with oregano

juice of 2 lemons
fresh or dried oregano
salt and pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut baking paper into four squares, about 20 cm each. (You can also use foil for this recipe.)
Put a piece of fish onto each square. Add 1 clove garlic, 2 teaspoons olive oil, a squeeze of lemon juice and a sprinkle of oregano to each. Season with salt and pepper then wrap up each parcel and bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
When ready, remove from the oven and transfer the contents of each packet to individual plates. Enjoy with a salad, rice, pasta, potatoes or vegetables. This would also be amazing with 1 teaspoon of Garlic dip (see below).

title: Garlic dip
ingredients:
1 cup garlic cloves, peeled
1 teaspoon salt
3 cups sunflower oil
½ cup lemon juice
steps:
Slice the garlic in half lengthwise and remove any green sprouts. Transfer to a food processor and add the salt. Process for a minute until the garlic becomes finely minced. Make sure to scrape down the sides of the food processor.
With the motor running, slowly pour in 1–2 tablespoons oil, then stop and scrape down the bowl. Continue adding another tablespoon or two until the garlic starts looking creamy.
Once the garlic looks emulsified, increase the speed of pouring the oil, alternating ½ cup oil with ½ cup lemon juice until all the oil and lemon juice are incorporated. This will take about 15 minutes.
Transfer the sauce into a glass container and cover with a paper towel. Place in the fridge overnight. The next day, replace the paper towel with an airtight lid and keep in the fridge for up to 3 months.

title: Chicken naked burger
ingredients:
500 grams chicken mince
2 spring onions, chopped
1 egg
½ cup rolled oats
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
⅓ cup cottage cheese
pinch of chilli flakes
salt and pepper
iceberg lettuce leaves (for the buns)
steps:
Mix together the chicken, onion, egg, oats, parsley, cottage cheese and chilli flakes, and salt and pepper to taste. Roll into patties and cook in a frying pan, on the BBQ or under the grill.
Serve in the lettuce leaf with the carrot, parsley and Homemade tzatziki .
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chicken souvlaki
ingredients:
4 chicken breast fillets, cubed
2 cloves garlic, crushed
juice of 1 lemon
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tablespoons dried oregano
salt and pepper
steps:
Place the chicken in a bowl with the remaining ingredients. Marinate in the fridge for about 1 hour.
Thread the chicken cubes onto the skewers and cook on the BBQ or under the grill for about 10 minutes.
Serve with a Greek salad.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean stuffed sweet potato
ingredients:
4 small sweet potatoes
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 carrots, grated
1 tomato, chopped
½ onion, finely chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon dried oregano
pinch of chilli flakes
400 grams beef mince
salt and pepper
2 tablespoons red wine vinegar
¼ cup chopped fresh coriander, to serve
steps:
Poke holes in each sweet potato with a skewer and microwave for 10 minutes, or bake in an oven at 180°C until cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the carrot, tomato, onion, garlic and spices until the onions are translucent. Add the beef and season with salt and pepper. Add ¼ cup water and cook for about 8 minutes. Stir through the vinegar.
Cut each sweet potato down the centre, scoop out some of the flesh. Add the flesh to the pan with the meat mixture.
Divide the meat mixture into the cavity of each sweet potato and garnish with coriander to serve.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Easy pork skewers
ingredients:
1 kg boneless pork, cubed
salt and pepper
1 tablespoon fresh or dried oregano
extra-virgin olive oil, for brushing
steps:
Thread the pork onto eight skewers and season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with the oregano and brush with some olive oil. Cook under the grill, on a BBQ or in a pan.
Serve with a garden salad.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Puttanesca with chicken
ingredients:
1 kg chicken pieces (or 1 whole chicken cut it into pieces)
salt and pepper
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
8 anchovy fillets
6 garlic cloves, crushed
2 tablespoons dried oregano
1 tablespoon dried basil
1 x 400-gram can peeled tomatoes
¼ cup capers (optional)
½ cup pitted black olives
pinch of chilli flakes
handful of fresh basil, to serve
steps:
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a frying pan and sear the chicken for about 10 minutes, turning regularly. Set aside.
Clean the pan and heat another 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Cook the anchovies, garlic and dried herbs and spices, then add the tomatoes, capers, half the olives and chilli if using.
Return the chicken to the pan and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes.
Serve with the remaining olives and basil scattered over the top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Stuffed capsicums with beef
ingredients:
4 red capsicums
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
400 grams beef mince
1 onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
1 x 400-gram can crushed tomatoes
½ cup basmati rice
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
½ cup chopped fresh mint
1 tablespoon dried oregano
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Slice the top off each capsicum and set aside. Remove the seeds and membrane.
Heat a dash of olive oil in a frying pan and cook the beef, onion and garlic. Add the tomatoes, rice and herbs, pour in ½ cup water, and cook for about 10 minutes over medium heat.
Divide the mixture evenly among the capsicums and put the lids back on top. Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 40 minutes.
When ready, remove from the oven and enjoy with a leafy green salad.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chicken salad with herbs and lemon
ingredients:
500 grams chicken thigh fillets
lemon wedges, to serve
steps:
For the marinade, put all the ingredients in a jar and shake well. Place the chicken in a dish, cover with the marinade and put in the fridge for 30 minutes.
For the salad, put all the ingredients in a really big salad bowl and toss to combine.
Cook the chicken by grilling, barbecuing or pan-frying. Let it rest for about 5 minutes then slice and arrange over the salad.
Serve the salad with lemon wedges.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Easy Greek meatballs
ingredients:
500 grams beef mince
500 grams lamb mince
4 cloves garlic, crushed
2 eggs
zest of 1 lemon
½ red onion, chopped
1 cup rolled oats
½ cup feta
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
2 tablespoons dried oregano
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary
salt and pepper
freshly squeezed lemon juice, to serve
chopped fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Mix all the ingredients together well. Roll tablespoons of the mixture into meatballs.
You can either fry the meatballs in olive oil or bake them in an oven at 200°C on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Serve with lemon juice drizzled over and scattered with fresh parsley. You can enjoy the meatballs with Homemade tzatziki and a green salad.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Moussaka
ingredients:
2 large eggplants
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for brushing
1 onion, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary
1 teaspoon allspice
pinch of chilli flakes
700 grams beef mince
2 x 400-gram cans crushed tomatoes
1 cup beef stock
¼ cup grated parmesan cheese
steps:
Cut the eggplant into 1 cm-thick slices, sprinkle with salt and let sit for about 20 minutes. Pat dry then brush with olive oil.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onion, garlic, rosemary, allspice and chilli until the onion is translucent. Add the beef and brown. Add the tomatoes and stock and cook for about 40 minutes to thicken.
While this is cooking, make the bechamel by melting the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and mix to a paste, slowly stir in the milk, then the nutmeg and cheese.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Assemble the moussaka in a baking dish with alternating layers of eggplant, meat sauce and bechamel. Repeat until everything is used up.
Sprinkle parmesan over the top and bake for 40 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Beef kofta
ingredients:
500 grams beef mince
1 onion, chopped
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
½ teaspoon ground allspice
½ teaspoon dried mint
salt
steps:
Mix all the ingredients together. You can do this in a food processor for a smooth consistency.
Shape the mixture around the skewers so they look like long rectangles. Leave the top and bottom of the skewers meat-free.
Put in the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up and set.
Cook on the BBQ or under the grill on medium heat until cooked through, about 10–12 minutes. Don’t turn too soon because they can fall apart, so wait until they’ve cooked a little before turning. Enjoy!
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean beef stew
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
600 grams diced beef
1 onion, sliced
6 cloves garlic, crushed
2 tablespoons chopped fresh rosemary
2 cups beef stock
2 cups chopped cherry tomatoes
2 capsicums, deseeded and chopped
2 x 400-gram cans butter beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup pitted black olives
2 tablespoons arrowroot flour
1 cayenne chilli, deseeded and chopped
steps:
Preheat the oven to 150°C. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a casserole dish and brown the beef over high heat. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the casserole dish and cook the onion, garlic and rosemary until the onion is translucent. Stir through the stock, tomatoes and capsicum. Return the beef to the dish and cook over low heat for 2 hours.
Add the beans and olives. Mix the arrowroot flour with some water and add it to thicken the stew. Simmer for another 20 minutes. Add the chilli just before the end of cooking time.
Serve with rice, cauliflower rice, mashed sweet potato or whatever you fancy.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Lamb shanks with beans
ingredients:
2 tablespoons arrowroot flour
salt and pepper
8 lamb shanks
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 onion, chopped
1 carrot, chopped
2 celery stalks, chopped
4 cloves garlic, crushed
1 x 400-gram can white beans, rinsed and drained
1 x 400-gram can crushed tomatoes
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary
2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
pinch of chilli flakes
1 cup beef stock
4 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
½ cup chopped fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Put the flour and some salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss the shanks through the seasoning. Add the olive oil to an ovenproof casserole dish and brown the shanks well over medium heat. Remove and set aside.
Put the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the casserole dish and cook until soft. Stir through the beans, tomato, rosemary, cinnamon and chilli. Pour in the stock and vinegar. Return the lamb to the dish, cover and roast in the oven for 1 hour.
When ready, remove from the oven and serve scattered with fresh parsley.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: One-tray Mediterranean chicken and veggies
ingredients:
4 chicken breast fillets
2 capsicums, chopped
2 zucchini, chopped
1 broccoli, cut into florets
½ red onion, chopped
1 lemon, cut into wedges
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Arrange the chicken and veggies on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Mix the seasoning ingredients together and sprinkle over the top. Bake for 25 minutes.
When ready to serve, scatter with the toppings and lemon wedges, and drizzle with olive oil.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chicken stew with okra
ingredients:
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
1 whole chicken, cut into pieces
500 grams chopped tomatoes (fresh or canned)
1 white onion, chopped
1 tablespoon red wine vinegar
1 teaspoon maple syrup
salt and pepper
500 grams okra
1 lemon, sliced
handful of fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a casserole dish and cook the chicken pieces for about 10 minutes, turning regularly to brown on all sides.
Add the tomatoes, onion, vinegar and maple syrup, and season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the okra and lemon to the chicken mixture. Drizzle with some olive oil and add some water if it looks dry. Cook for another 20 minutes.
When ready, garnish with parsley and serve with a Greek salad, pita breads or rice.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: BBQ lamb cutlets with mango cheeks
ingredients:
2 mangoes, sliced into cheeks
8 lamb cutlets
salt and pepper
1 teaspoon extra-virgin olive oil
steps:
Score the mango cheeks with a noughts and crosses grid. Season the lamb with salt and pepper.
For the dressing, put all the ingredients in a jar and shake well.
Heat the olive oil on a BBQ or hotplate, and cook the lamb and mango until the mango looks golden brown and the lamb is cooked to your liking.
Serve with the mango cheeks turned out and dressing drizzled over the lamb.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mediterranean roast lamb
ingredients:
2.5 kg leg of lamb
salt and pepper
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2 onions, sliced
2 capsicums, chopped
6 cloves garlic, crushed
2 cups chicken stock
1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
10 sprigs of fresh thyme
4 bay leaves
1 cup chopped cherry tomatoes
½ cup pitted kalamata olives, to serve
lots of fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 130°C.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper then place on a baking tray or in a roasting dish with the olive oil. Cook over high heat to brown the meat. Remove the meat and set aside.
Add the onion, capsicum and garlic to the tray and cook until soft. Add the stock and vinegar.
Return the lamb to the tray and add the thyme and bay leaves. Cover and bake for 6 hours on the oven’s lowest setting. Add the tomatoes in the last hour.
When ready, remove from the oven, scatter with olives and parsley, and serve.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Simple lamb with potatoes
ingredients:
1.5 kg leg or shoulder of lamb
juice of 3 lemons
1 teaspoon dried oregano, plus extra to season
salt and pepper
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
1.5 kg potatoes, chopped into quarters
steps:
Preheat the oven to 150°C. Place the lamb in a roasting pan. Rub the lemon juice all over the lamb, sprinkle with the oregano and season with salt and pepper. Pour the olive oil over and put in the oven for about 2 hours.
Check the lamb every 30 minutes, basting and turning over as needed. If the lamb is looking a bit dry, add some water to the pan.
At the 1 ½-hour mark, add the potatoes to the pan. Season with oregano, salt and pepper, and drizzle some more olive oil over. Cook for another hour, so 2 ½ hours all up.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Lemon and rosemary pork chops
ingredients:
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
4 bay leaves
4 cloves garlic, crushed
2 lemons, thinly sliced
4 pork chops
salt and pepper
⅓ cup chicken stock
1 tablespoon fresh rosemary leaves
handful of fresh parsley, to serve
steps:
Heat the olive oil in a casserole dish, add the bay leaves and garlic and cook. Set aside.
Put the sliced lemons in the dish with the bay-infused oil and cook until golden. Set aside.
Season the pork chops with salt and pepper and cook for a few minutes until golden. Pour in the stock and return the garlic, bay leaves and lemon to the dish. Add the rosemary and cook on low for 30 minutes.
When ready, garnish with fresh parsley and serve with a salad, some rice or baked vegetables.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Beef-stuffed eggplant
ingredients:
4 eggplants, cut in half lengthwise
salt and pepper
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil
500 grams beef mince
4 spring onions, chopped
500 grams chopped tomatoes (fresh or canned)
½ cup chopped fresh parsley, plus extra to serve
2 tomatoes, sliced
1 cup grated parmesan cheese
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Sprinkle the eggplant halves with salt and set aside for about 1 hour. Drain any excess water.
Heat 1–2 tablespoons olive oil in a frying pan and brown the eggplant. When browned, put the eggplant in an ovenproof dish, skin side down.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in the pan and cook the beef and spring onion. When the mince is browned, add the chopped tomatoes and parsley.
Scoop out a cavity in each of the eggplant halves. Add the beef mixture evenly into the cavities, arrange slices of tomato on top and sprinkle with parmesan.
Add ½ cup of water to the dish and bake in the oven for 45 minutes.
When ready, serve scattered with parsley and seasoned with salt and pepper.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Dolmades
ingredients:
500 grams vine leaves (canned or fresh) (see note)
500 grams beef mince
1 onion, grated
⅔ cup basmati rice
⅓ cup chopped fresh parsley
⅓ cup chopped fresh dill
150 ml extra-virgin olive oil
2 eggs
juice of 4 lemons
salt and pepper
steps:
If using fresh grape leaves, blanch them in boiling water for a couple of minutes. If using fresh cabbage leaves, do the same.
Put the beef, onion, rice, herbs and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a bowl. Use your hands to combine well.
Lay some of the leaves in the bottom of a frying pan. Take a leaf and place it shiny side down on a work surface. Grab about 1–2 tablespoons of the meat mixture and place it in the leaf. Roll it tight, folding in the sides as you go.
Pack the leaf parcels neatly into a casserole dish standing up side by side. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Pour in 1 cup boiling water.
Cover the dolmades with an inverted plate to keep them in place, and simmer for about 45 minutes.
When the dolmades are ready, beat the eggs and lemon juice together, along with any extra pan juices. Pour the egg mixture over the dolmades and let rest for about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
If you can’t find vine leaves, cabbage leaves work just as well. You will need up to 40 leaves to be on the safe side.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Pistachio biscotti
ingredients:
3 ½ cups almond flour
½ cup chopped pistachios
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
pinch of salt
2 eggs
½ cup butter, softened
½ cup honey
½ teaspoon vanilla extract
steps:
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients.
Scatter flour on a work surface. Turn out the dough and form into rectangular-shaped loaves. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool for about 20 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 120°C.
Slice the loaves into biscotti and bake until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Almond paximathia
ingredients:
2 cups almond flour
½ cup chopped roasted almonds
2 teaspoons baking powder
1 tablespoon orange zest
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
½ teaspoon ground ginger
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
pinch of salt
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil
½ cup honey
juice of 1 orange
sesame seeds, for topping
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients. Let the mixture rest for about 20 minutes.
Scatter flour on a work surface. Turn out the dough and form into cylinders. Score the tops, scattering with sesame seeds. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 120°C.
Cut the cylinders into slices and bake until just golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Sarah’s breakfast paximathia
ingredients:
3 cups almond flour
½ cup cocoa powder
2 teaspoons baking powder
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
pinch of salt
1 cup shelled pistachios
1 cup dark chocolate chips
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil
juice of 1 orange
½ cup black coffee (you can make this with instant)
½ cup honey
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients.
Scatter flour on a work surface. Turn out the dough and form into logs. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool for 20 minutes, then drop the temperature to 120°C.
Cut the logs into 1.5 cm slices and bake until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Artichoke flatbread
ingredients:
4 Basic flatbreads
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for brushing
juice of ½ lemon
1 tablespoon Greek yoghurt
100 grams goat’s cheese
60 grams feta
2 cups rocket leaves
1 capsicum, deseeded and sliced
1 cup jarred artichoke hearts, drained
½ cup pitted black olives
½ cup chopped cherry tomatoes
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Brush your flatbreads with olive oil and bake for 5 minutes.
Mix the lemon juice, yoghurt and cheeses together with the olive oil. Spread the mixture over the warmed flatbreads then add the rocket, capsicum, artichokes, olives and tomatoes. Bake for another 5 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Orange, honey and olive oil paximathia
ingredients:
2 cups almond flour
1 teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil
½ cup honey
juice of 2 oranges
zest of 1 orange
⅓ cup slivered almonds
2 tablespoons sesame seeds, for scattering on top
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients, making a dough.
Scatter flour on a work surface. Turn out the dough and form into two logs. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, allow to rest for 10 minutes, then drop the temperature to 120°C.
Slice the logs into biscotti and bake until golden brown, about 15–20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool.
