title: Olive oil and honey cookies
ingredients:
1 ½ cups almond flour
1 cup rolled oats
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon ground cloves
½ teaspoon baking powder
pinch of nutmeg
pinch of salt
1 cup raisins
1 egg
½ cup honey
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tablespoons hot water
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 teaspoon sea salt, for sprinkling
steps:
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients and the raisins in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients to make a dough.
Form into cookies, using 2 tablespoons of mixture per cookie. Flatten a little using a fork and sprinkle with sea salt. Bake until brown, about 12 minutes.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool on the baking tray and enjoy!
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Classic Greek rusks
ingredients:
2 ½ teaspoons dry yeast
½ teaspoon maple syrup
450 grams almond flour
pinch of salt
1 ½ cups lukewarm water
steps:
Put the yeast in a small bowl with ½ cup water and the maple syrup, and mix together. Allow to sit for 10 minutes to activate the yeast.
Put the flour in a bowl with the salt. Add the activated yeast and knead the dough mixture for 5 minutes. Add the water gradually – your goal is to not end up with a sticky dough. Shape into a ball and let it sit for about an hour.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Form the dough into a log shape and make 3 cm-long cuts crosswise on the top. Bake for 1 hour.
Remove from the oven then lower the temperature to 100°C.
Slice the dough into rusks and bake for another hour or until completely dry.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Bean flatbread casserole
ingredients:
olive oil cooking spray
2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 x 400-gram cans black beans, rinsed and drained
4 cloves garlic, crushed
½ cup vegetable stock
2 tablespoons chopped fresh coriander
1 teaspoon ground cumin
salt and pepper
1 ½ cups Sarah’s easy salsa , or store-bought salsa
1 cup grated cheese
4 wholegrain flatbreads (store-bought is fine)
Greek yoghurt, to serve
fresh herbs, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Spray a casserole dish or cake tin with olive oil cooking spray.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the beans and garlic for a few minutes. Stir in the stock, coriander and cumin, and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the bean mixture, salsa and half the cheese among the four flatbreads. Roll up and place in the bottom of the casserole dish. Scatter the remaining cheese on top. Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
When ready, serve with yoghurt and fresh herbs of your choice.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Basic flatbread
ingredients:
140 grams wholemeal self-raising flour
220 grams Greek yoghurt
1 teaspoon salt
steps:
Mix the flour, yoghurt and salt in a bowl. Shape into a ball and let it rest for 30 minutes.
When rested, divide the dough into four pieces. Roll each piece into a circle shape with a rolling pin.
Heat a pan, ideally cast iron, and cook each dough circle for a few minutes on each side. The flatbread will puff up and char, which is normal.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Homemade pita bread
ingredients:
4 cups wholemeal flour
1 tablespoon dry yeast
1 ¼ cups warm water
½ teaspoon sea salt
steps:
Preheat the oven to 250°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix together the flour and yeast, add the water and salt, and mix together to form a dough. Knead for 5 minutes or until the dough is smooth.
Form into 10 balls. Roll each ball into a circle shape and set aside on the tray to rise for 30 minutes.
Just before you put them in the hot oven, flip them over. Bake for 5 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Feta and zucchini muffins
ingredients:
4 zucchini
2 eggs
100 grams feta, crumbled
½ onion, finely chopped
1 ½ cups almond meal
3 tablespoons chopped fresh or dried parsley
2 tablespoons grated parmesan cheese
2 tablespoons chopped fresh or dried dill
2 tablespoons chopped fresh or dried mint
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Brush a muffin tray with olive oil then line with baking paper or muffin cases.
Grate the zucchini, place in a bowl, sprinkle with salt and let it sit for about 10 minutes. Squeeze out the excess water and set aside.
Mix the remaining ingredients in a large bowl and add the zucchini. Combine, then scoop into the muffin cases and bake until golden brown, about 30 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Flatbread with a Greek influence
ingredients:
1 ½ cups warm water
1 tablespoon active dry yeast
2 cups wholemeal flour
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon dried rosemary
steps:
For the dough, mix the water and yeast together and let stand for 10 minutes.
Add 1 cup of the flour and the olive oil, salt and dried herbs. Knead slowly, adding the remaining flour. Let rise for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Grease a baking tray and line with baking paper.
When ready, roll out the dough into a flatbread shape. Place the dough on the tray and brush with olive oil. Spread the tomato, onion and salt and pepper over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes and serve with the feta and basil.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Classic pizza base
ingredients:
1 ⅓ cups warm water
1 tablespoon yeast
1 tablespoon honey
3 ½ cups wholemeal plain flour
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 teaspoon salt
steps:
Whisk the water with the yeast and honey and let sit for 5 minutes.
Put the flour, olive oil and salt in a stand mixer and mix at a low speed for about 3–5 minutes. Add the yeast.
Tip out onto a lightly floured work surface and knead the dough for 5–10 minutes. This makes a thick dough. Cover with plastic wrap and let sit for at least an hour until the dough has doubled in size.
When ready, you should be able to punch it down. At this stage, you can wrap it to freeze for another time, or it is ready to roll out for your favourite toppings.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Cauliflower pizza base
ingredients:
750 grams cauliflower florets
½ cup grated cheese
1 egg
salt and pepper
dried herbs of your choice (optional)
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Grate the cauliflower florets using a box grater or pulse in a food processor. Microwave for 5 minutes to cook. (If you don’t have a microwave, you can cook the cauliflower in a pan over low heat for about 6 minutes.) Let cool.
Grab a tea towel or a nut-milk bag if you have one. Put the cauliflower in the tea towel and squeeze out the excess water.
Put the cauliflower in a mixing bowl and add the cheese and egg, and stir to make a dough.
Line a baking tray with baking paper and spray with olive oil. Shape the cauliflower into a pizza base and bake in the oven for 25 minutes.
Remove from the oven and load up with your favourite toppings (see page 276 for ideas).
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Broccoli pizza base
ingredients:
1 head broccoli, cut into florets
1 egg
3 cloves garlic, crushed
½ cup almond meal
½ cup grated mozzarella
¼ cup grated parmesan cheese
2 teaspoons salt
1 teaspoon fresh or dried oregano
pinch of pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Add the broccoli to a food processor and pulse until it looks like rice. Grab a tea towel or nut-milk bag if you have one and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Put the broccoli in a bowl with the remaining ingredients and mix to combine. Shape into four mini-pizzas or one big pizza. Bake for about 30 minutes.
Remove from the oven and load up with your favourite toppings (see page 276 for ideas).
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Sarah’s tomato sauce
ingredients:
2.5 kg fresh tomatoes
1 white onion, chopped
2 cloves garlic, crushed
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
bunch of fresh basil
pinch of sea salt
cracked black pepper
dried chilli flakes, oregano or honey to sweeten (optional)
steps:
Boil a pot of water. Once the water is boiling, add the tomatoes. Boil for about a minute until the skins split. Remove and immediately place in cold water. Once cool enough to touch, remove the skins.
In a large saucepan sauté the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon olive oil until transparent.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining ingredients to the saucepan, including the other tablespoon of olive oil. Cook on very low heat for about an hour, stirring occasionally.
If you have a handheld blender then blitz. Otherwise, transfer the ingredients to a blender. Once blended, place into freezer bags and freeze until needed.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Crustless pumpkin pie
ingredients:
250 grams feta, crumbled
1 egg
½ cup milk of your choice
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
salt and pepper
500 grams butternut pumpkin, peeled and deseeded
2 cups almond flour
honey, to serve
handful of fresh thyme, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish or cake pan with olive oil.
Mix 150 grams of the feta, egg, milk, olive oil, and salt and pepper to taste. Grate the pumpkin into the mixture, and add the almond flour until it forms a dough.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish (ideally the mixture needs to be about 2 cm high). Crumble the remaining feta over the top and bake for 50 minutes.
Serve with a drizzle of honey and sprinkle of thyme.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: No-pastry cheese pie
ingredients:
2 eggs
150 ml milk
½ cup Greek yoghurt
150 grams cheddar cheese, grated
100 grams feta, crumbled
250 grams almond flour
45 ml extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for greasing
2 tablespoons fresh or dried thyme
pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a cake tin with olive oil.
Whisk together the eggs, milk and yoghurt in a bowl.
In another bowl, mix the cheeses with the flour. Add the olive oil, thyme and pepper to taste, then mix together the wet and dry ingredients to make a batter. Bake for 30 minutes.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Zucchini pie
ingredients:
3 cups grated zucchini
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup feta, crumbled
1 cup grated cheddar cheese
3 spring onions, sliced
¼ cup chopped fresh mint
1 teaspoon fresh or dried oregano
2 cups almond flour
4 eggs
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 teaspoon baking powder
steps:
Put the grated zucchini in a strainer or colander with the salt and let it sit for about 45 minutes. Press down into the strainer to squeeze out the liquid.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Put the cheeses, onion, mint and oregano in a bowl. Mix through the zucchini. Add the flour, eggs, olive oil and baking powder, mixing well. Bake in the oven for about 1 hour.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Apple crumble cake
ingredients:
⅓ cup rolled oats
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon maple syrup
steps:
Preheat the oven to 175°C. Grease a 22-cm square baking dish.
For the crumble, mix all the ingredients together.
For the cake, place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients. Add the apples and coat well in the mixture. Tip into the baking dish and bake for about 40 minutes.
Remove from the oven, dot the crumble on top and return to the oven to bake for another 10 minutes.
When ready, serve with yoghurt.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Cheesy honey-baked pears
ingredients:
2 fresh pears
4 tablespoons gorgonzola or blue cheese (or any cheese you like)
4 teaspoons crushed walnuts
4 sprinkles of fresh thyme
4 cups rocket leaves
4 tablespoons honey
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the pears in half lengthwise and remove the cores, making a cavity in each. Place the pear halves, skin side down, on the tray.
Divide the gorgonzola, walnuts and thyme evenly among the pear halves, then bake for 8–10 minutes.
Meanwhile, make a bed of rocket on a serving platter.
Remove the pears from the oven, arrange on the rocket and drizzle with the honey.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Lemon and olive oil cake
ingredients:
2 ⅓ cups almond flour
½ cup tapioca flour
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
salt
3 eggs
juice and zest of 2 lemons
⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
lemon zest, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Grease a round springform cake tin and line with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients.
Bake for 25–30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Turn out onto a cooling rack. When cool, scatter lemon zest over the top, and enjoy with some Greek yoghurt or on its own with a cup of tea.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Fruit cake
ingredients:
400 grams mixed dried fruit
1 ½ cups almond flour
½ cup coconut flour
2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
2 teaspoons mixed spice
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda
pinch of salt
¾ cup chopped walnuts
juice and zest of 1 orange
5 eggs
¼ cup coconut oil
1 tablespoon vanilla extract
steps:
Soak the fruit in boiling water for about 20 minutes until it becomes soft. You can use any dried fruit you choose – dates, sultanas and cranberries are my top choices. Drain and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 150°C. Line a round cake tin with baking paper.
Place the dry ingredients in a large bowl. Add the walnuts and orange zest and mix together. In another bowl, whisk together the wet ingredients. Slowly combine the wet into the dry ingredients.
Fold in the softened dried fruit. Pour mixture into the cake tin and bake for about 1 hour or until a skewer poked in the centre comes out clean.
Turn out onto a cooling rack. Cool and enjoy.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Chocolate figs
ingredients:
400 grams fresh figs, chopped
2 tablespoons almond butter
1 cup dark chocolate chips
2 teaspoons coconut oil
sea salt, to serve
steps:
Line a baking tray with baking paper. In a food processor, combine the figs and almond butter with a dash of water. Roll the mixture into balls, placing them on the baking tray.
Melt the chocolate chips and coconut oil in the microwave or in a glass bowl over a saucepan of boiling water. Dip the fig balls into the melted chocolate and replace them on the baking tray.
Sprinkle with some sea salt and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes. This is a cute snack for when you’re on the go.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Carrot cake with honey and olive oil
ingredients:
½ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for brushing
2 ½ cups almond flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon ground ginger
pinch of salt
3 eggs
2 cups grated carrot
½ cup Greek yoghurt
½ cup honey
⅓ cup milk
6 dates, pitted and chopped
½ cup chopped walnuts
steps:
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Brush a 20 x 20 cm square baking dish with olive oil then line with baking paper.
Place all the dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, mix together the wet ingredients, then fold into the dry ingredients. Fold in the dates and walnuts. Bake for 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
Cool and cut into squares. Enjoy!
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Baked ricotta figs
ingredients:
500 grams ricotta
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for greasing
4 tablespoons honey
4 fresh figs, quartered
pinch of salt and pepper
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish with olive oil.
Put the ricotta in a bowl and give it a good stir, then transfer to the baking dish. Sprinkle with the rosemary, half the olive oil and half the honey. Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, add the figs and salt, and return to the oven for another 5 minutes.
Remove from the oven and drizzle with the remaining olive oil and honey plus salt and pepper to taste. Serve with a green salad and maybe some toasted sourdough.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Peach tarte
ingredients:
1 ½ cups rolled oats
1 cup chopped pitted dates
1 tablespoon coconut oil
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
zest of 1 lemon
pinch of salt
500 grams Greek yoghurt
1 teaspoon honey, plus extra to drizzle
1 teaspoon vanilla bean paste
4 peaches, sliced
steps:
Blitz the oats, dates, coconut oil, vanilla extract, lemon zest and salt in a food processor. Press into the bottom of a pie dish and put into the fridge to set.
Mix the yoghurt, honey and vanilla bean paste together in a bowl and pour over the tarte base. Set in the fridge for 2 hours.
When ready to serve, remove from the fridge. Top the tarte with the sliced peaches and a drizzle of honey and serve immediately.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Peaches, apricots and yoghurt
ingredients:
4 peaches, pitted and cut into wedges
4 apricots, pitted and cut in half
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
1 cup Greek yoghurt
2 tablespoons honey
juice of 1 lemon
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
¼ cup roasted pistachios, to serve
handful of fresh mint, to serve
steps:
Toss the peaches and apricots in the oil then grill for a minute on each side.
In a bowl, mix the yoghurt, honey, lemon juice and vanilla extract.
Add the grilled fruit to a serving plate and dollop with the yoghurt. Garnish with pistachios and mint.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Labne with berries and pistachios
ingredients:
750 grams Greek yoghurt
3 teaspoons vanilla bean paste
zest of 1 orange
¼ cup honey
1 teaspoon rosewater
½ teaspoon saffron
500 grams blueberries
150 grams blackberries
¼ cup toasted pistachios
steps:
To make the labne, place the yoghurt, 2 teaspoons vanilla bean paste and orange zest in a cloth (I use a muslin tea towel) placed over a bowl. Tie it up tight and put it in the fridge for about 24 hours.
The next day, put the honey, 1 teaspoon vanilla bean paste, rosewater, saffron and ½ cup water in a saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer for about 1 minute.
Mix the berries into the rosewater mixture and put in the fridge to chill.
When ready to serve, place a dollop of labne at the base of 4 individual glass dishes, followed by the rosewater berries and finally top with toasted pistachios.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Sarah’s easy yoghurt cake
ingredients:
olive oil cooking spray
1 ½ cups Greek yoghurt
4 eggs
⅓ cup tapioca flour
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease an 18 cm springform cake tin with cooking spray and line with baking paper.
Whisk together the yoghurt and eggs, then add the flour and vanilla to make a smooth batter. Pour into the tin and bake until golden brown, about 50 minutes.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool; it will deflate. Put in the fridge for 2–3 hours to set.
When ready to serve, top with your favourite toppings and enjoy.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Baked apples
ingredients:
⅓ cup butter, plus extra for greasing
4 apples
juice of 1 lemon
⅓ cup maple syrup
½ cup chopped walnuts
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon ground cloves
Greek yoghurt, to serve
steps:
Preheat the oven to 150°C. Grease a baking dish with butter.
Cut the top off each apple and remove the core, being careful not to cut all the way through to the base. Rub lemon juice all over the apples. Put the apples in the baking dish and add ⅓ cup water to the dish.
Mix together the butter, maple syrup, walnuts and spices. Fill the apples with the spice mixture and bake in the oven for about 1 hour. Keep checking them, refilling the apples with the spice mixture every 10–15 minutes as needed.
Remove from the oven and serve with yoghurt.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Coffee cupcakes
ingredients:
½ cup almonds
2 eggs
½ cup honey
2 teaspoons mixed spice
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon instant coffee
1 cup almond flour
½ teaspoon baking powder
⅓ cup chopped walnuts
1 tablespoon sesame seeds
steps:
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a muffin tray and line with paper cases.
Blitz the almonds in a food processor.
In a bowl with a mixer, beat the eggs, honey and spices until thick, about 10 minutes. Add the olive oil and coffee, then the ground almonds, almond flour and baking powder.
Add to the muffin tray, sprinkle with walnuts and sesame seeds, and bake for 20 minutes.
Cool in the tin, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Poached pears with a nut crunch
ingredients:
½ cup honey
1 vanilla bean, split
8 pears
2 cups frozen blueberries
Greek yoghurt, to serve
fresh mint, to serve
ground cinnamon, to serve
steps:
Put the honey, vanilla and 1 litre of water in a deep saucepan or casserole dish. Bring to the boil, add the pears, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes. They still need to be firm but not mushy. Add the berries and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes.
Remove the fruit to a plate.
For the crunch, mix the honey and almonds together. Put in a frying pan and heat for about 2 minutes. Once the almonds look caramelised, remove from the heat and let cool. Chop into pieces.
Serve on individual plates with pears at the base and nut crunch on top. Garnish with yoghurt, mint and a sprinkle of cinnamon.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Sweet quinoa and fruit
ingredients:
1 cup cooked quinoa
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon mixed spice
pinch of salt
juice and zest of 1 orange
¼ cup honey
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
2 peaches, cut into wedges
1 orange, peeled and cut into wedges
1 cup Greek yoghurt
⅓ cup toasted walnuts
2 tablespoons passionfruit pulp
bunch of fresh mint
steps:
Mix the quinoa with the spices and a tiny pinch of salt. Stir through the orange juice and zest, honey and olive oil.
Divide the mixture among 4 little bowls. Add the peach and orange wedges and yoghurt, then scatter with walnuts, passionfruit pulp and mint over the top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Pomegranate, rosemary and lime summer refreshments
ingredients:
2 limes, thinly sliced
1 pomegranate, seeds only
bunch of fresh rosemary
1.25 litres mineral water
juice of 4 limes
1 tablespoon honey
steps:
Place a lime slice in each hole of an ice-cube tray, then cover with 1 teaspoon pomegranate seeds and a small rosemary sprig. Fill with water and place in the freezer to set.
Mix the mineral water, lime juice and honey together in a jug.
Add the pomegranate ice cubes to individual glasses and pour the mineral water mixture over the top.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Tahini crumble with fruit
ingredients:
extra-virgin olive oil, for greasing
4 peaches, sliced
2 nectarines, sliced
1 cup pitted fresh cherries
1 tablespoon butter
juice of 1 lemon
1 tablespoon honey
steps:
Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish with olive oil.
Place the fruit in the bottom of the dish. Mix together the butter, lemon juice and honey. Pour over the fruit and bake for about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine the crumble ingredients in a bowl.
Remove the fruit from the oven, dot with the crumble mixture and return to the oven for another 30 minutes. Enjoy!
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Cinnamon, fig and banana nice cream
ingredients:
6 ripe figs, frozen
4 ripe bananas, frozen
2 tablespoons honey
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
steps:
Put all the ingredients in a food processor and blitz well. You may need to add a dash of water to get it moving along.
Empty into a container and freeze.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub
file_path: books\added\My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Coffee frappe
ingredients:
6 ice cubes
½ cup water
1 teaspoon instant coffee granules
1 teaspoon honey (optional)
steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender and blitz to combine.
source: My Mediterranean Life _ Recipes and stories.epub

title: Mango and yoghurt ice blocks
ingredients:
2 cups chopped fresh mango
juice of 1 lime
1 cup Greek yoghurt
¼ cup honey
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
steps:
Put the mango and lime juice in a blender and blitz. Pour into 6 ice-block moulds and freeze for 30 minutes, to harden slightly.
Whisk together the yoghurt, honey and vanilla. Remove the moulds from the freezer, add the yoghurt mixture and return to the freezer until firm.
